name: Primary Interstitial Lung Disease Specific to Childhood Due to Alveolar Structure Disorder
aliases: Childhood Interstitial Lung Disease due to Alveolar Dysplasia
Pediatric Alveolar Structure Disorder Interstitial Lung Disease

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Childhood Interstitial Lung Disease Diagnostic Criteria

criteria.description: Progressive respiratory distress and hypoxemia in infancy or early childhood
High-resolution CT showing diffuse interstitial lung abnormalities with alveolar simplification
Lung biopsy demonstrating alveolar simplification and abnormal alveolar architecture
Identification of mutations affecting alveolar development genes (if available)
Exclusion of infectious, immunologic, and other known causes of interstitial lung disease

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of progressive respiratory symptoms with characteristic radiologic and histopathologic findings, and exclusion of other causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing may support diagnosis but is not mandatory; lung biopsy remains gold standard.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Failure to thrive secondary to respiratory insufficiency
searchTerms: poor growth due to breathing problems
failure to thrive from respiratory issues
signs of high blood pressure in lungs

rare.symptomName: Peripheral edema due to right heart failure
searchTerms: swelling in legs from heart problems
ankle puffiness due to heart failure

rare.symptomName: Chest wall deformities secondary to chronic respiratory disease
searchTerms: chest deformities from chronic lung disease
abnormal chest shape due to breathing problems
chest wall changes from lung illness

laboratory: Arterial blood gas showing hypoxemia and respiratory alkalosis
Normal or mildly elevated inflammatory markers
imaging: High-resolution CT demonstrating diffuse alveolar simplification and interstitial thickening
Chest X-ray showing reticulonodular pattern and hyperinflation
genetic: Mutations in genes regulating alveolar development (e.g., NKX2-1, SFTPC) in some cases
other: Lung biopsy confirming alveolar architectural abnormalities and interstitial fibrosis

distinguishingFeatures: History of prematurity and oxygen therapy
Radiologic findings of cystic changes rather than alveolar simplification
Genetic testing positive for surfactant protein mutations
Histopathology showing alveolar proteinosis or desquamative interstitial pneumonia

redFlags: Severe hypoxemia refractory to oxygen therapy
